topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how previously learned concepts will be integrated.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and tissue injury by matching conserved microbial and damage patterns to genetically encoded host receptors.

topics.label: PRR families, downstream signaling, and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major classes of pattern recognition receptors, their spatial intracellular signaling cascades, and the multi-protein inflammasome mechanism for cytokine processing.

topics.label: Cellular inflammatory response, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow the immediate cellular cascade of inflammation from sentinel cell activation and leukocyte extravasation into tissues to lymphatic drainage and systemic septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic persistence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, how tissues are repaired, and the consequences of persistent inflammation such as fibrosis and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
